Relatório Circunstanciado de Identificação e Delimitação: Terra Indígena Nawa, Mâncio Lima - Acre. Brasília: Funai. 313 pp. (posted under 'contestações administrativas').
sources.note: Nothing on stress or tone and no word list (full text searched: acento 0, sílaba 0, fonolog 0, tônic 1 = 'tectônica', vocabul 2, língua 15). Section I(a) 'filiação cultural e linguística' places the Nawa in the 'conjunto etnolinguístico Pano' (Erikson 1992; map after Erikson 1992 and Aguiar 2018) and states (p. 57) that several self-identified Nawa command 'um considerável vocabulário Pano' but nobody speaks the language fluently, with a recent 'retomada' by passing on known vocabulary and borrowing Pano terms from other groups. Incidental items only: personal name Mariruni (p. 78), awá 'anta…

Read in the work dir, not kept (non-linguistic).

sources.citation: Rivet, Paul & Constant Tastevin. 1929. Les dialectes Pano du haut Juruá et du haut Purús (fin). Anthropos 24(3-4): 489-516. [Part 2 of the comparative vocabulary (entries d-v) plus errata to part 1 (Anthropos 22, 1927: 811-827); Nawa forms labelled '(5) Nawa du P. Tastevin'.]
sources.note: Wordlist-only: about 37 Nawa verb forms across the two parts (part 2 has 22, e.g. 'être debout bani (5)', 'marcher tape (5)', 'nager nuné (5)', 'chanter tiri (5)', 'chercher béna (5)'), several printed with an acute accent, but the article's transcription key defines only two consonant letters and says nothing about accent; the only remark on Nawa is (part 1, p. 816 fn.) that Nawa and Kanawary are represented by too few words to enter the comparison. No stress or tone statement exists in either part; part 2 was the unread 'open online, not downloaded' works still to obtain and is now obtained.

sources.citation: Rivet, Paul & Constant Tastevin. 1927. Les dialectes Pano du haut Juruá et du haut Purus. Anthropos 22: 811-827 (continued in Anthropos 23-24, 1928-1929).
sources.note: Nothing on Nawa accent. p. 814: Nawa word list collected in situ by Tastevin; p. 816 fn.: 'Le Nawa et le Kanawary sont représentés par trop peu de mots pour qu'on puisse les faire entrer en ligne.' Phonetic remarks concern Kashinawa/Kapanawa sound correspondences only.

sources.citation: Tastevin, Constant. 1919. Quelques considerations sur les indiens du Jurua (seance du 6 novembre 1919). Bulletins et Memoires de la Societe d'Anthropologie de Paris, VIe serie, 10: 144-154. doi 10.3406/bmsap.1919.8875
sources.note: No description of nawa1239. One incidental remark on the accent of a single word, the generic ethnonym: 'Je crois, de plus, qu'il faut considerer le suffixe na comme l'abreviation de nawa.. assez facile a s'expliquer quand on pense que l'accent tonique du mot nawa [printed nâwa] se trouve sur la penultieme, et qu'on prononce plus souvent naw que nâwa.' (p. 152). This is about how Pano speakers/settlers of the Jurua pronounce the word nawa, not a word-stress rule for the Moa Nawa language; recorded here so nobody mistakes it for one. Rest of the article: locations, demography, material culture…

sources.citation: Tastevin, Constant. 1914. En Amazonie. Sur le Moa, aux limites extremes du Bresil et du Perou. Les Missions catholiques 46: 502-504, 514-516, 526-528, 537-539, 550-552, 559-561. [cited in ISA Povos Indigenas no Brasil, 'Nawa', Fontes de informacao]
sources.note: No phonology content and no Nawa vocabulary. The only language remark in the article (f517): 'Leur nom, les Nucuinis, éveilla mon attention. Quand on sait que, dans la langue indigène, l'l et l'r s'interchangent fréquemment, on constate que ce nom est celui même des Roucouyennes de la Guyane française' — a speculative ethnonym etymology, nothing on accent; f513 'chantent en leur langue bizarre' (porters). Negative evidence only.
